messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 3589 - continuous-batcher error spike in us-west-2. latency > 3s for 90th pct, queue depth climbing, multiple pods reporting OOM and CUDA failures. paging oncall group now.

maya: i'm on it. seeing batch_size growth on the metric dashboard — accumulator length trending upward for the last 2m.

liam: logs from a node show repeated CUDA failures and container restarts. snippet:```
2026-03-15T12:34:10Z runtime[pid=2345]: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION at runtime/kernel.c:412
2026-03-15T12:34:11Z runtime[pid=2345]: oom-killer invoked, killing process 2345 (batcher)
2026-03-15T12:34:12Z kubelet: Container runtime restarted container batcher-abc on node ip-10-0-12-34
```

aj: i can confirm a node-flap — ip-10-0-12-34 bounced once and came back with container crash loop. CPU spiked on prefetch thread.

runtime-ops: quick question — is the continuous-batcher rollout from yesterday? any recent config changes to prefetch or kv-cache?

maya: we rolled 2026-03-14 23:10 UTC with aggressive prefetch (kv_prefetch=4 -> 12) and larger accumulators. early telemetry was fine but at scale in us-west it's runaway.

sre-bot: small impact detected: 47 requests/min failing 502, tail latency jittered to 8s for some customers. Synthetic canaries in prod saw increase in token latency.

emily_support: Support reports two customers (CUST-374, CUST-912) seeing elevated latencies and occasional 503s in the last 10 minutes. They are flagged as enterprise.

liam: attaching minimal repro log for the crash:```
[ERROR] BatchAccumulator overflow: size=16384 limit=8192
[TRACE] batcher::enqueue at batcher.rs:128
[TRACE] batcher::process at batcher.rs:256
[ERROR] runtime: failed to allocate KV cache, returning OOM
```

maya: immediate mitigation suggestion: 1) scale down continuous-batcher replicas to 0 for affected nodepool, 2) disable aggressive prefetch via feature-flag, 3) roll back to previous batcher image which had backpressure fix.

aj: planning to cordon ip-10-0-12-34 and drain. i'll also trigger a k8s rollout pause for the batcher deployment in us-west-2.

runtime-ops: giving commands to execute:```
# cordon and drain node
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-34
kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force -n inference
# scale batcher down in affect pool
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/continuous-batcher --replicas=0 --context=aws-us-west-2
# toggle feature flag (ff) in configmap
kubectl -n infra patch configmap/ff-continuous-batcher -p '{"data":{"kv_prefetch":"6"}}'
```

maya: i'm going to open an emergency rollback PR and post the image hash here. if we can get batcher back to previous image we should see queue depth return to normal.

aj: node cordoned and drain started. one pod terminated forcibly due to OOM during drain. watch logs for restarts.

sre-bot: incident-bot update: fail count trending down after scale down actions, but a residual 10% tail latency remains.

liam: fwiw, GPU page faults were observed prior to the illegal instruction. hypothesis: kernel/cuda driver mismatch on one node combined with larger KV cache allocations -> page thrash -> OOM -> crash loop.

runtime-ops: can we fallback routing to smaller model variant to reduce memory pressure? product-ops: any objections to temporary routing?

product-ops: ok to route to small-2 model for non-SLA traffic and keep enterprise pinned to dedicated capacity if needed. coordinate with support to notify customers.

emily_support: notifying affected customers and offering a mitigation note. raising priority for CUST-374 and CUST-912.

maya: rollback PR merged, new deployment image: ghcr.io/redwood/batcher@sha256:abcd1234 -> rolling out. reverting kv_prefetch to 4 via configmap.

aj: scale up batcher in canary (2 pods) with old image in us-west, monitoring.

sre-bot: canary observed: queue depth stabilizing, OOMs stopped on canary pods.

liam: still seeing node ip-10-0-12-34 with low-level driver errors — recommending we drain and reprovision that instance.

aj: node fully drained and cordoned. setting autoscaling to avoid scheduling on it. raising infra ticket to reprovision.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE - containment achieved. rollback + drain + feature-flag reduced failures to baseline. SEV changed to mitigated.

emily_support: posting status update to customers and to status.redwood.ai: "We experienced elevated latency and intermittent 5xxs in us-west-2 due to a batching runtime bug. Immediate rollback and node remediation mitigated the issue. Engineers are investigating root cause."

maya: next steps: 1) permanent revert or fix for accumulator bounds (add strict backpressure), 2) add e2e test for prefetch scaling, 3) monitor kv_prefetch metric via alert at lower threshold, 4) schedule postmortem.

product-ops: please include customer impact timeline and the list of affected enterprise customers in the postmortem.

liam: saving logs and heap dumps to s3://redwood-incident-archive/3589124000/ for postmortem.

runtime-ops: attendees for handoff to day team: maya, liam, aj, emily_support. leaving a detailed runbook in the incident doc.

maya: handing off — i'll be available for follow-ups but switching to oncall-2. leaving links: metrics dashboard https://dashboards.redwood.ai/r/cont-batcher-us-west, logs https://logs.redwood.ai/q/3589124000, incident doc https://incidents.redwood.ai/3589124000.

aj: acknowledged, taking over watch for next 2 hours.

sre-bot: thread closed for oncall rotation. keep the channel updated if regressions. :white_check_mark:
